data.ruling: The refutation does not stand. Only the datasheet verifier refuted, and the stock verifier confirmed every figure. The requirement is written at Monostable.md@23c82ca:232-234 and IOBoard.md@e13f5f6:194: "A part whose clear release can trigger is excluded; the '423-type behaviour, where clear release never triggers, is required and is stated in the datasheet." The Nexperia 74HC423 datasheet Rev. 8.1 states that behaviour in two places. Section 1 says: "The '423' is identical to the '123' but cannot be triggered via the reset input." Table 3, the function table, has no row that fires a pulse when nRD rises. The 74HC_HCT123 datasheet Rev. 13 carries exactly that row in its Table 3 (nRD rising, nA L, nB H, one pulse), so Nexperia left it out of the '423 table on purpose. The verifier's reading of Fig. 9 is correct. In the 74HC423 datasheet, Fig. 9 (drawing mna522, nA = LOW) shows nQ rising at the second nRD release while nB is HIGH and staying high for a full tW. Drawing mna522 is the same artwork, under the same drawing ID, as Fig. 9 on page 12 of the 74HC_HCT123 datasheet. It is a '123 illustration carried over into the '423 datasheet. It contradicts the '423 datasheet's own general description and function table, and those two govern. The verifier itself says that "the Nexperia datasheet states the behaviour". The requirement asks that the behaviour be stated in the datasheet. It does not ask for a datasheet free of contradicting drawings, so "not stated without ambiguity" is a reading the page does not contain. TI's CD74HC423 datasheet (SCHS155, revised October 2003) supports the family distinction: "the 123 types ... triggered by a negative to positive reset pulse; whereas the 423 types do not have this feature", and it draws a separate '423 waveform as Figure 2. The part stays. The contradiction is recorded against it and goes to the owner. Test step 5 of Monostable.md@23c82ca:547-553 settles it on the bench, where a pulse one window after the rail settles excludes the part, and so would a written statement from Nexperia. A latch that powers up set (V29, for research) would also hold the gates through such a pulse. The scope is function: the refutation is about this function's clear-release requirement, not about the part's lifecycle, maker or LCSC identity.
data.evidence: 74HC423 Rev. 8.1 (13 March 2024), section 1: "When nRD is LOW, it forces the nQ output LOW ... and also inhibits the triggering ... The '423' is identical to the '123' but cannot be triggered via the reset input." Table 3 rows: (L,X,X) gives Q L; (X,H,X) gives Q L [1]; (X,X,L) gives Q L [1]; (H,L,rising) gives a pulse; (H,falling,H) gives a pulse. There is no nRD-rising row. Fig. 9, page 9, rendered at 200 dpi, drawing ID mna522, caption "Output pulse control using reset input nRD", nA = LOW: nB rises and then stays HIGH, nRD goes low and is released, and nQ rises at that release and stays high for tW. So the figure does show a pulse fired by the reset release. 74HC_HCT123 Rev. 13 (21 February 2024): its Table 3 has the extra row (nRD rising, nA L, nB H) giving a pulse. Its Fig. 9 on page 12, rendered at 150 dpi, is the same drawing, mna522, with the same waveforms. That makes the '423 figure a carried-over '123 drawing that contradicts the '423's own text and function table. TI CD74HC423 (SCHS155, revised October 2003), front page: "They are all ... triggered by a negative to positive reset pulse; whereas the 423 types do not have this feature." Its Figures 1 and 2 are separate reset-control drawings. Requirement: Monostable.md@23c82ca:229-236 and IOBoard.md@e13f5f6:194 ("stated in the datasheet"). Test step 5: Monostable.md@23c82ca:547-553. Stock verifier: confirmed, no failed checks.
